card.title: Equations of uniform acceleration
card.body: $$v = u + at, \quad s = \left(\dfrac{u+v}{2}\right)t, \quad s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2, \quad s = vt - \dfrac{1}{2}at^2, \quad v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
card.says: five equations linking displacement $s$, initial velocity $u$, final velocity $v$, constant acceleration $a$, and time $t$ — each one leaves out a different variable.
card.from: combining the definition of constant acceleration ($v = u + at$) with the mean speed theorem ($s = \dfrac{u+v}{2}\,t$).
card.useWhen: motion is along a straight line with **constant acceleration**. List the three quantities you know and the one you want, then pick the equation missing the fifth.
card.example: A train starts at $u = 4\text{ m/s}$ with constant $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$ for $t = 5\text{ s}$. Then $v = 4 + 2(5) = 14\text{ m/s}$ and $s = 4(5) + \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(5^2) = 20 + 25 = 45\text{ m}$. Check: $v^2 = 14^2 = 196 = 4^2 + 2(2)(45)$.
card.analogy: Five different wrenches for the same five-variable toolbox: pick the one that does not need the variable you neither have nor want.
